provenanceNote: AUTHORED, not extracted. tracker-lock.mjs has no existing test pinning lockDirFor's key derivation, so each expected value was produced by running the live implementation rather than taken from a pre-existing verified assertion. This file proves a second implementation AGREES with the current JS derivation; it does not prove that derivation is independently correct.
why: A cross-process lock only excludes if every implementation derives the SAME lock directory from the same tracker path. Backoff and retry timing may differ harmlessly; the NAME may not. Two implementations that disagree here do not contend at all — both believe they hold the lock and write the user's applications.md concurrently. That is silent corruption, not a visible failure. This is the half of the lock protocol expressible as input -> output, and it is the half that decides whether mutual exclusion exists at all.
notCovered: Acquisition retry/backoff, stale-lock recovery windows and the recover-guard handshake are sequenced and clock-dependent, so a case table cannot express them. They still rest on convention across the three implementations. Also not covered: the CAREER_OPS_TRACKER_LOCK override validation (absolute + inside temp root + correct prefix, because release deletes recursively). The rule is real and both sides implement it, but the JS form is a private helper taking an env value and a lock key against the live filesystem, while the Kotlin form is a pure three-boolean predicate. There is no shared callable shape to pin, and a fixture the reference implementation cannot answer does not belong in a shared corpus.

lockKey.note: macOS temp-style path, the shape real test roots take

non-ASCII path: pins UTF-8 byte agreement across languages
